short: Noise-augmented self-supervised AVSR training (M03) was new in 2022 but rests on one test set with no run count; the 49.6% babble gain mixes data and model size with pre-training.
position: The paper [@shi2022robust] changes training (M03): self-supervised audio-visual pre-training with noise in pre-training and fine-tuning. The authors claim a first, and none of the 143 AVSR ledger studies dated before it pre-trains self-supervised or adds noise in pre-training (Appendix); M03 is still standard because both effects rest on one test set with no run count or seed reported (Sec. 3.1). M12 is standard: like most of the field it reports no variability, although a test-set interval as in [@makino2019rnnt] needs no extra training. The 49.6% babble gain over [@xu2020discriminative] measures the whole recipe (unlabelled data, LARGE model, 30 h against 433 h of labels), not robustness from pre-training. At the same 30 h budget, later pseudo-labelling reaches 2.2% against 3.3% clean AVSR WER without noise augmentation [@haliassos2026usr2].
